content: Adverse reactions to oral penicillin V potassium are less frequently reported compared to those associated with parenteral penicillin therapy. However, it is important to note that all degrees of hypersensitivity reactions, including life-threatening anaphylaxis, have been documented with oral penicillin use. The most commonly reported adverse effects of oral penicillin include nausea, vomiting, epigastric discomfort, diarrhea, and the development of a black hairy tongue. Hypersensitivity reactions associated with oral penicillin may manifest as skin eruptions, ranging from maculopapular rashes to exfoliative dermatitis. Other hypersensitivity reactions include urticaria, serum sickness-like reactions, laryngeal edema, and anaphylaxis. In some cases, fever and eosinophilia may be the only observed reactions to oral penicillin. Less commonly, adverse effects such as hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, neuropathy, and nephropathy have been reported. These reactions are typically associated with the administration of high doses of parenteral penicillin rather than oral formulations.
